topic: How much salt is too much

scenes.line: Never add salt? You may still eat too much.
scenes.visual: Flat poster salt shaker on an apricot block with a bold ink strike through it; small salt grains gather in a little pile beside it
scenes.animation: Block wipes up from the bottom at start; shaker drops in on 'salt'; strike draws across on 'Never' timing; grains pile up with 0.05 s stagger on 'still'

scenes.line: The WHO says adults should eat less than 5 grams of salt a day.
scenes.visual: Big teal block with a huge serif '< 5 g' and an ink chip 'WHO' plus a small label 'salt a day'
scenes.animation: Chip pops on 'WHO' (back.out); block scales up from 0.8 on 'less'; number slides up on '5'; label fades on 'day'

scenes.visual: Flat teaspoon with a small white salt mound that stops just below the brim, on the paper background
scenes.animation: Spoon slides in from the left on 'That's'; salt mound grows from 0 on 'under', stopping short of the brim line

scenes.line: The NHS says no more than 6 grams.
scenes.visual: Two blocks side by side: teal 'WHO < 5 g' (already known) and a new apricot block 'NHS 6 g max'
scenes.animation: WHO block slides left and shrinks at start; apricot block rises in on 'NHS'; '6 g' number pops on '6'

scenes.line: Guidelines differ, so ask your doctor what's right for you.
scenes.visual: The two blocks tilt slightly apart; an ink speech bubble below reads 'Ask your doctor'
scenes.animation: Blocks rotate a few degrees apart on 'differ'; speech bubble pops with back.out on 'doctor'

scenes.line: Around three quarters of the salt we eat is already in food we buy,
scenes.visual: Ink block with a huge serif '¾' and a flat pie chart: three of four slices filled apricot, one slice paper
scenes.animation: Block wipes in at start; pie slices fill one by one, stagger 0.15 s, on 'three'; label 'in food we buy' fades on 'buy'
scenes.onScreenText: About ¾ is already in food

scenes.line: like bread, breakfast cereals and ready meals.
scenes.visual: Three flat food tiles in a column: a bread loaf, a cereal bowl, a ready-meal tray, each with an ink chip label
scenes.animation: Tile 1 pops on 'bread', tile 2 on 'cereals', tile 3 on 'ready' (back.out, 0.3 s each)

scenes.line: Too much salt can raise your blood pressure, which increases the risk of heart attacks and strokes.
scenes.visual: Flat half-circle gauge on a paper panel with a needle that moves from teal toward the rose end; two calm ink chips below: 'Heart attack risk' and 'Stroke risk'
scenes.animation: Gauge arc draws at start; needle rotates toward rose on 'raise'; chips slide up on 'heart' and 'strokes'

scenes.line: One easy step: check the label and pick the lower-salt option.
scenes.visual: Two flat food packets with front labels: left label shows a rose 'Salt: HIGH' bar, right shows a teal 'Salt: LOW' bar; a magnifier and a tick on the right packet
scenes.animation: Packets slide up at start; magnifier sweeps across on 'label'; right packet scales up with a tick on 'lower-salt', left packet dims

scenes.line: Save this for your next shop, and talk to your doctor if you're watching your blood pressure.
scenes.visual: Teal block with a bookmark icon and a flat shopping basket; ink chip 'Talk to your doctor' below
scenes.animation: Bookmark drops and bounces on 'Save'; basket slides in on 'shop'; chip pops on 'doctor'

scenes.onScreenText: Not medical advice. Sources: WHO, NHS, CDC
